Linnaeus-era taxonomists relied on incomplete sketches and travelers’ tales. Even early genetic studies struggled to resolve their family, leading to placement in the unique family Ailuridae. Juvenile observations confirmed unique behaviors that didn’t fit raccoon or bear analogies. This prolonged taxonomic limbo highlights challenges of classifying enigmatic, rare species. Evolutionary isolation in Himalayan forests contributed to a mosaic of traits. Today, red pandas remain the only living members of their family, a zoological oddity that defied early scientific expectations.

IMPACT_PARAGRAPH_2: It underscores how morphology alone can mislead scientific understanding.
